correctness.rationale: A nonresolving set lies within a pair bisector; hence its largest possible size is the maximum bisector size. For mixed complete-graph Cartesian products, the probability of equal distances is exactly the zero-sum probability for independent increments with masses (1/q_i, (q_i-2)/q_i, 1/q_i). Convolution maximum-atom bounds, ternary equality support, and decreasing central binomial probabilities give the stated exhaustive maximizing coordinate supports. Distinct bisectors then correspond to coordinate fibers, binary parity classes, ternary permutation graphs, and binary–ternary two-cell patterns, with the announced exact counts. The script independently verifies 61 profiles/82,284 vertex pairs and directly checks all subsets of critical size when N<=12; the unlimited proof is not based on these experiments.

value.rationale: Every arbitrary landmark sample of this critical size resolves a mixed-alphabet Hamming network, independently of its placement. The theorem identifies sharp 1/3-versus-1/2-versus-(q-2)/q phase transitions, classifies all worst-case indistinguishable pairs and exactly counts the largest failing sets. Robust worst-case placement and failure multiplicity are natural questions distinct from minimal metric bases; the binary/ternary exceptional equality structure explains the phenomenon.
